5,300 lb, after deducting the main block, ball and rigging
5,500 lb, after deducting the main block and the ball
7,000 lb, since the jib chart already shows a net load
rationales: This leaves out the main block. The chart note requires deducting it when the block stays reeved at the boom head.
7,000 − 1,200 − 300 = 5,500 leaves out the 200 lb of rigging, which is part of the load.

beyond: The idle main block hangs at the boom head and still loads the boom, which is why charts deduct it even though it is not on the whip line.
fact: When lifting on a jib, deduct the main hook block left reeved at the boom head, plus the overhaul ball and rigging.

misconceptions: Hoist line assumed to carry the entire weight
beyond: This ideal balance calculation does not include dynamic forces or establish an approved erection procedure.
